title: Rudy Powell's Benny Goodman imitation ruins his embouchure
summary: Rudy tried Goodman's growl, developed a whistle in his tone that spoiled Victor sides, and was replaced by Sedric.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: And he wouldn't have asked for the world, because he was tickled to death to be in the band, and he was playing damned good, and the only thing ruined him then, hurt him, I would put it, he was wrapped up in -- uh -- Benny Goodman playing.
Trying to play like Benny Goodman.

Yes. Yes. And Rudy always did study. He's had some very, very fine teachers, and he knows the instrument, the alto, and he's very good on the clarinet, but he's terrific on the alto. That's always been the way -- you know.

And so I think I heard them -- I've heard it discussed by different clarinet players, the growl -- growling or growl, or whatever you want to call it, that Benny Goodman has done on the clarinet then. A few guys seem to -- to think it was great.
Sounds like a kind of dirty tone.

Yeah, so Rudy was messing with that, so he ruined his embouchure. He -- while playing it, he, whew! -- dah, dah, dah, whew! You know? He had that whistle sound would come out, and that happened on too many Victor wax.
They spoke about it a few times, and after a while they said well -- (slap) -- you know, I'm sorry, but get somebody else. Then they brought in Eugene Sedric.
See, that's -- because Rudy was there before Eugene Sedric, see?
So it was because of Rudy's problem with his embouchure that --
Yeah, it was that whew, ssss, ssss, whew! You know. They said we can't have that, have to start again, and start again, and start again, and --

Was this -- you remember the way -- well, for example, the way Ben Webster used to play? Had a sort of breathy sound to it, because he got very close to the mike? Now is this what Rudy was doing? Or was it more of a whistle?
That was a whistle, because you could hear it while he was playing, you know. Everything would be

nice for four, five, eight, or ten notes, dah, dah, dah, wssst! De, dah, dah dah, dah, wsst! You know. I mean a definite -- you know. And you could hear it in there. It ruined -- well, it ruined things.
And that's one of the things that hurt him, you know?
